executive_summary: Bajaj Auto’s September quarter supports its export, premium-motorcycle and electric-mobility growth engines. The key analytical trap is comparing the management discussion of the core standalone business with consolidated revenue, debt and cash flow that include a different business mix.
research_stance: A stronger core and EV business, with consolidated balance-sheet and KTM complexity requiring separate valuation work.
results_analysis: The local consolidated September 2026 quarter records revenue ₹25,126.00 crore, operating profit ₹4,896.00 crore and PAT ₹3,384.00 crore. Revenue changed +59.7% YoY and +15.8% QoQ; PAT changed +59.5% YoY and +6.1% QoQ.

Operating profit changed +73.1% YoY and +8.1% QoQ. The calculated operating-profit/sales margin is 19.49%, versus 17.98% a year earlier and 20.88% in June. These calculations use a consistently rounded local series; management EBITDA may use a different scope or definition.

The stored consolidated quarter has ₹25,126 crore revenue and ₹3,384 crore PAT. Management’s core discussion cites approximately ₹20,000 crore revenue, ₹4,172 crore EBITDA and 20.9% margin, on a different scope. Do not reconcile these by mixing standalone margin with consolidated sales. September consolidated borrowings of ₹26,401 crore require subsidiary-level analysis rather than interpreting them as the manufacturing business debt.

Price and financial dates differ: the cleaned close used here is ₹10,945.00 on 2026-11-12; the public-financial snapshot is dated 2026-11-13. The screenshot price is not treated as a live or verified valuation input. Local public-financial-data parquets, September 2026 quarter; amounts rounded to ₹ crore.

Audit clarification: management calls the combined EV business, including three-wheelers, margin-accretive, while the CFO separately describes electric two-wheeler mix as still dilutive. These statements have different product scopes. Consolidated growth also includes Bajaj Mobility with a one-quarter reporting lag and a changed year-on-year base.

thesis_drivers.title: Export recovery with share gains
thesis_drivers.evidence: Management reported exports of about 7.8 lakh units and strong African and Latin American demand. Geographic diversification helps, but Nigeria and currency availability remain cyclical exposures.

thesis_drivers.evidence: Chetak market share reached 23% per management and the overall EV business was margin-accretive at corporate level. Capacity and service execution now matter more than treating EV as a distant loss-making option.

thesis_drivers.evidence: Pulsar launches and KTM/Triumph broaden the 125cc-plus franchise. Management is deliberately protecting margin rather than chasing entry-segment volume, so total domestic share alone is an incomplete performance gauge.

industry_context.content: Evaluate motorcycles, electric scooters, commercial three-wheelers, exports and overseas investments separately. industry_context.heading: Growth versus price paid
industry_context.content: The cleaned close implies about 23x available consolidated trailing EPS, but KTM/overseas consolidation and finance subsidiaries make a core-business-plus-investments SOTP more informative. Illustrative P/E cases below use the available group EPS only and are sensitivity checks, not a substitute for that SOTP.

valuation.method: Reverse valuation and cash-earnings constraints; no unsupported point target
valuation.assessment: The approximately 23× price/available-group-EPS ratio appears more modest than many watchlist names, but the earnings perimeter is changing. Motorcycles, exports, Chetak, BACL and KTM need appropriate economic measures and capital claims. Consolidated P/E alone cannot establish whether the core franchise is cheap.
assumptions: At the 12 November adjusted close of ₹10,945.00, the available four-quarter EPS sum is ₹469.85, implying approximately 23.3× earnings and a 4.29% earnings yield. This is a price/available-EPS calculation, not a forecast or a fully normalized multiple.

A 20% contraction in the earnings multiple would require 25% cumulative EPS growth merely to keep the share price unchanged; dividends are excluded. This is algebraic sensitivity, not a prediction of the exit multiple.

A genuine SOTP requires core cash flow, finance-company book and credit costs, overseas ownership, debt/guarantees and restructuring adjustments. Unexplained terminal multiples do not replace this work.

quality_assessment.management: Rakesh Sharma described a deliberate trade-off: protect profitability in 100cc motorcycles while investing in premium Pulsar, exports and Chetak. Dinesh Thapar’s core cash-flow disclosure is useful, but management’s record requires a separate test of KTM/overseas capital deployed versus cash and returns delivered to Bajaj shareholders.

quality_assessment.governance: Promoter ownership increased from 55.01% in June to 55.95% in September; the reason for the change was not independently reconstructed. KTM/overseas exposure and finance subsidiaries require scrutiny of guarantees, intercompany funding, acquisition accounting and board-approved investment limits before treating the core franchise’s cash as fully distributable.

claim_audit.claim: September 2026 revenue ₹25,126.00 crore and PAT ₹3,384.00 crore.
claim_audit.assessment: The live canonical table agrees with the report input. Revenue, total PAT and EPS must retain their respective accounting definitions. This is an internal canonical-table check, not an assertion of independent auditor verification.

claim_audit.claim: Core EBITDA was ₹4,172 crore and margin 20.9%; consolidated revenue was ₹25,126 crore.
claim_audit.assessment: These have different reporting perimeters. Dividing core EBITDA by consolidated revenue would create a fictitious margin.

claim_audit.claim: Bajaj Mobility/KTM is consolidated with a one-quarter reporting lag.
claim_audit.assessment: The prior-year comparator did not include the same full quarter. Reported group growth is not like-for-like manufacturing growth.

claim_audit.claim: Q2 exports reached 7.8 lakh units, up 41%, with a forward aim around 7.5 lakh per quarter.
claim_audit.assessment: The forward operating aim is not a contracted export order book; regional demand and currency availability remain cyclical.

claim_audit.claim: Chetak share reached 23%; combined EV profitability includes electric three-wheelers.
claim_audit.assessment: The combined EV profitability statement explicitly includes three-wheelers, so it should not be attributed solely to Chetak.

claim_audit.claim: The CFO separately says electric two-wheeler mix still dilutes overall margin.
claim_audit.assessment: This qualifies the broader combined-EV statement. A favourable three-wheeler mix does not prove Chetak alone is margin-accretive.

claim_audit.claim: Chetak capacity is targeted at 80,000 units monthly, but timing references differ.
claim_audit.assessment: Prepared remarks say Q4; later Q&A says next quarter. The schedule inconsistency remains open.

claim_audit.claim: PLI accruals benefited from a rate change, with an 18% exit rate described for H2.
claim_audit.assessment: The maximum rate transition is not automatically a fresh incremental margin step each quarter. Accrual and cash collection can also differ.

claim_audit.claim: Core quarterly PAT was ₹3,354 crore, with nearly ₹4,000 crore company-defined FCF.
claim_audit.assessment: This cash measure is a core-period disclosure; it cannot be combined with group borrowings as though on the same perimeter.

claim_audit.claim: KTM H1 revenue was €701 million and adjusted EBITDA €38 million.
claim_audit.assessment: Management notes restructuring-profit adjustments. The turnaround needs a recurring operating and cash reconciliation.

claim_audit.claim: BACL had about ₹21,000 crore AUM and ₹243 crore quarterly PAT.
claim_audit.assessment: The financing subsidiary changes group funding and profit mix. Its debt is not equivalent to factory leverage.

claim_audit.claim: Input inflation remained material despite pricing and operating leverage.
claim_audit.assessment: Stable quarterly margin does not demonstrate that raw-material risk has disappeared.

claim_audit.claim: FY26 operating cash flow ₹2,597 crore; dataset free cash flow ₹1,885 crore.
claim_audit.assessment: Annual cash-flow figures were re-read; they are not September-quarter or H1 cash flows and do not use management-adjusted FCF definitions. This is an internal canonical-table check, not an assertion of independent auditor verification.

The reported percentage agrees with the local ownership table; any change in percentage requires a corporate-action/share-count bridge before describing it as promoter buying or selling. This is an internal canonical-table check, not an assertion of independent auditor verification.

business_economics: Exports, premium domestic motorcycles and electric mobility are separate growth engines. Q2 exports of 7.8 lakh units and 23% Chetak share support scale, but regional demand, foreign-currency availability and capacity/service execution are different constraints.

The central EV nuance is product mix. Management calls the combined EV business, including three-wheelers, margin-accretive; the CFO separately says growing electric two-wheelers still dilute overall margin. Treating the combined statement as proof of Chetak margin accretion would overstate unit economics.
earnings_quality: The core business reports ₹4,172 crore EBITDA at 20.9% margin; the consolidated group reports ₹25,126 crore revenue. These numbers must not be combined to calculate a margin. Group year-on-year growth also includes a full quarter of Bajaj Mobility on a changed comparable base and with a one-quarter lag.

Other operating income includes export incentives, PLI accruals and genuine-oil royalties. The PLI exit rate moves to 18% according to management; that supports current profit but is not a new rate step in every future quarter. Nearly ₹4,000 crore core quarterly FCF is strong, although working-capital and accrual-to-cash effects need separate tracking.
capital_allocation: BACL reported about ₹21,000 crore AUM and ₹243 crore quarterly PAT. Its funding changes group debt interpretation: ₹26,401 crore consolidated borrowings are not automatically industrial net debt, while core cash is not automatically distributable before guarantees and intercompany funding are assessed.

KTM’s €38 million adjusted H1 EBITDA and positive Q2 EBIT are early turnaround evidence. The shareholder test is recurring cash after restructuring and capital committed, rather than accounting consolidation or one positive quarter.
valuation_logic: About 23× available consolidated EPS mixes manufacturing, financing and an overseas turnaround. A sector P/E on blended earnings risks double-counting value or missing funding claims.

A SOTP should value core cash, BACL risk-adjusted book returns and KTM normalized operating cash separately, then account for attributable debt, guarantees and future capital. Until that bridge exists, a precise target grid would overstate confidence.
peer_positioning: Domestic motorcycle peers help compare premium share, volume, realizations and core margins. Electric-scooter peers help compare distribution and service, but their valuation does not establish Bajaj’s EV value. Financing and KTM require separate comparables.

Exports diversify demand, but regional recovery and incentives can make a current run-rate appear more permanent than it is. Compare through-cycle volume and cash generation rather than assuming every future quarter repeats the current export performance.
